claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was born c. 185 and died c. 254, and was the most important theologian and biblical scholar of the early Greek church.
Origen's Commentary on the Gospel of Matthew originally comprised 25 books.
Only Books 10-17 of the Commentary on Matthew have survived whole in the original Greek.
The Commentary on Matthew dates from AD 244 or after, making it one of Origen's latest works, along with Contra Celsum.

According to Eusebius, the Commentaries on the Gospel of Matthew were written about the same time as the Contra Celsum, when Origen was over sixty years of age, and may be assigned to the period 246-248.
Books 10-17 cover the portion from Matthew 13:36 to 22:33.
Book 15 covers Matthew 19:12-20:16, including the three types of eunuchs, Jesus' ministry to little children, the rich young ruler, and the parable of the hired workers.
Until recently, no English translation of the Greek text of Books 15-17 had been produced, though the Ante-Nicene Fathers series contains a translation of Books 10-14.
